deep_summary: Most people never think about the monitor they use. But not you. If you work from home as I do, your monitor is your window into your trade, whether that's scrolling through endless spreadsheets or color grading short films. Different work has different needs, and finding the monitor that suits your specific use case can be tricky with all the options out there. But with over a decade of testing and reviewing monitors under my belt, here are my recommendations on what you should buy today. For more information, check out our guide to How to Choose a Monitor, as well as our recommendations for Best Gaming Monitors, Best Portable Monitors, and Best Cheap Monitors. Dell Amazon Dell It's worth spending more than a hundred bucks on your monitor. Whether it's to improve image quality, upgrade sharpness through higher resolutions, or to add extra ports, you'll want something that makes your daily work life more pleasant. That's why I recommend the Dell 27 Plus 4K as the monitor most people should buy. Unlike many 4K monitors, the Dell 27 Plus 4K sells for under $300 (oftentimes as low as $280), despite being quite bright and color-accurate for an IPS panel at this price. It even comes with a fast 120-Hz refresh rate. I like this feature, especially since higher refresh rates are becoming more commonplace on phone and laptop screens. The only real downside to the Dell 27 Plus 4K is that the port selection is woefully limited. The two HDMI ports and one DisplayPort are enough for the basics, but if you have a laptop without HDMI, like a MacBook Air, you'll need a USB Hub or laptop docking station. For a more versatile monitor, I'd recommend upgrading to the model with a built-in USB hub (S2725QC). The QC model is identical, except that its extra USB ports make this monitor a far better fit for a connected home office. Dell does charge you $50 more for those ports, but for some, it'll be worth the convenience. Either way, you'll be hard-pressed to find a cheaper 4K monitor of this quality or a better monitor for under $300. Dell Amazon B&H Dell If you are looking for a larger, more fully featured home office monitor meant to sit at the center of a workstation, I'd recommend the Dell UltraSharp 32 4K (U3225Q). This thing is a beast. It's got just about every port and feature you can imagine, including a Thunderbolt-compatible USB-C port with power delivery up to 140 watts, an Ethernet jack, and a built-in KVM switch. This fully eliminates the need for a separate laptop docking station. Beyond that, it delivers on image quality in a big way. It uses IPS Black for enhanced color accuracy and contrast, and at the time of testing, it had the best image quality of any IPS display I'd tested. It's not OLED, but the 120-Hz UltraSharp U3225Q is impressively bright in SDR, maxing out at well over 400 nits in my testing. You're paying a lot for the extra functionality and image quality, so make sure you actually need it before pulling the trigger on this over the 27-inch model. There are plenty of 32-inch monitors out there if extra size is all you're looking for. Just remember, at 32 inches, anything under 4K isn't going to look sharp. But even 4K doesn't come close to the sharpness of something like a MacBook Pro. That's where the BenQ 27-inch 5K (MA270S) enters the picture.
